changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 2.0.14[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]New: Personal Assistant[/COLOR]
-luc_kodi now has a personal assistant that greets you when you open it, tells you how your accounts and scrapers are doing, and takes over Search: you type a title or ask in your own words, it finds it, tells you what sources there are and in which resolution, and plays the one you choose. It uses the add-on's own icon and has its own section in Settings.
[COLOR fffdb515]Personal Assistant: welcome summary[/COLOR]
-Opening luc_kodi greets you over the main menu with a short summary: good morning, afternoon or evening with your name, the accounts you have signed in and the state of your scrapers.
-Accounts shows the logo of every active service with a green dot, or orange when a subscription ends within 7 days or a tracker needs signing in again, and says which. It is the same check as System status, and expiry dates are refreshed in the background so the window opens straight away.
-Scrapers shows the last test and how long ago it ran (All 9 scrapers are working normally, or 7 of 9 with the ones that need a look). Opening never tests them, so it costs no requests. The last result is kept across restarts.
-Check again tests your enabled scrapers against one popular film, with a progress bar, and refreshes the accounts. You can close the window meanwhile: the test finishes and its result is kept. It shares the provider test's lock and cooldown, so the two never overlap.
-Close or Back closes it. It only appears when luc_kodi is opened in the Videos window: never from a skin widget on the home screen, never during playback, and not on the first opening after an update, when the changelog is shown.
[COLOR fffdb515]Personal Assistant: Search[/COLOR]
-Search in the main menu opens the assistant's own window: one field where you type a title or ask in your own words, Look in (Everything, Movies or TV Shows), your recent searches and the classic searches (Search Movies, Search Shows, by actor). More search options opens the old Search menu, AI Search included. The search in the context menu does not change.
-A title (Titanic, Titanic 1997, play Titanic in 4K) is looked up on TMDb. It is opened straight away only when there is nothing to choose: one title with that exact name and none starting with it, or a query that says which one (a year, play ..., in 4K). Otherwise the picker shows them all, the exact title first and selected (Titanic, Titanic II, Raise the Titanic...).
-It finds as many titles as the classic search: it asks for as many as Title Search limit (Movies and TVShows), the same setting the classic search uses, in pages of 20. Part of a title (rise of gru) lists the titles holding every word first, then the rest found. Empty TMDb entries (no date, no votes) are left out.
-A title ending in a number that looks like a year (Blade Runner 2049, Wonder Woman 1984) is searched as that title, not as the older film of that year.
-Is everything working? (or check my scrapers, status) opens the welcome summary with your accounts and scrapers.
[COLOR fffdb515]Personal Assistant: sagas[/COLOR]
-Searching a saga by its name (Rambo, Avatar, Minions, Mission: Impossible) lists every film of it first, oldest first and numbered (Movie · 2 of 5), with the film of that exact name already selected, and then every other title found (Minions & More, Minions: Holiday Special...), with a line saying how many of each.
-A film of the saga can be asked for by its number: Rambo 2, Rambo II, Rambo part 3, rambo primera parte, second Avatar. It opens that film in release order (Rambo 1 is First Blood). A saga with no film called just that (Harry Potter) lists its films too.
-One film of a saga typed by its own title (Rambo III, Blade Runner 2049), or a title with its year (Titanic 1997), opens straight away.
-Sagas come from TMDb's collections, and only films already released are listed.
[COLOR fffdb515]Personal Assistant: TV shows[/COLOR]
-A TV show opens its own sheet: poster, number of seasons and episodes, whether it is still running, the latest episode and the next one with their dates.
-What would you like to watch? Continue (the episode after the last one you watched, from your Trakt or SIMKL progress), Latest (the last episode aired) or First episode, and your seasons, specials last. A season lists its aired episodes with their pictures and dates. Back in that list returns to the sheet. All seasons and episodes opens the usual seasons list.
-Episodes can be asked for in the search: Silo s3e1, Silo 3x01, Silo season 3 episode 1, las fierbinti temporada 2 capitulo 5. Silo season 2 lists the episodes of that season. An episode not aired yet says so instead of searching.
[COLOR fffdb515]Personal Assistant: in your own words with Gemini[/COLOR]
-A request that is not a title (a 90s sci-fi movie with aliens) is read by Gemini, when you have Gemini keys, and TMDb answers it with the same Discover query as AI Search. The titles open in the assistant's picker under Here's what I found, with what Gemini understood (I understood: Movie · Science fiction · 1990–1999 · aliens), in as many pages as Title Search limit asks for.
-The title you pick goes on like any other: a film to its guided results, a TV show to its sheet. A resolution in the request (... in 4K) is kept.
-When Gemini cannot answer, or nothing matches, the assistant says why instead of opening an empty list. Asking Gemini... is shown while it thinks. Without Gemini keys, the classic title search shows what TMDb finds.
[COLOR fffdb515]Personal Assistant: its own picker[/COLOR]
-Every choice the assistant asks for opens in its own window, in the same style as the rest of the assistant, instead of Kodi's list: titles as a row of posters with their year, and the episodes of a season as a row of pictures with their dates. A title with no poster on TMDb shows a frame with its name instead of an empty space.
-The title you are on is described in full below the row: its whole title, a line with the year, Movie or TV show, its place in the saga (2 of 5 in the saga), and its plot, which scrolls by itself when it is longer than two lines. For an episode: S03E01 · date and the episode's plot.
-Ratings are shown with their icons beside the title: IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, TMDb and Trakt, each in its own colour. TMDb's appears at once; the others come from the same ratings as the sources list (MDBList, Trakt and OMDb with your key), asked in the background for the title you stop on and kept for 24 to 48 hours, so moving along the row is never slowed down. A rating that a site does not have is simply not shown.
-OK opens it, Back closes it. Back in a season's episodes returns to the show's sheet.
[COLOR fffdb515]Personal Assistant: guided results[/COLOR]
-After the search for sources, a film or episode opened from the assistant shows a summary instead of the long list: Here are your results, how many sources from how many scrapers and which ones, and how many in 4K, 1080p, 720p and SD, each in its own colour. An episode is headed with the show, the episode and its title (Silo · S03E01 · Who Are You?).
-Which resolution do you prefer? One button per resolution found, with its number of sources, plus Best available and All sources. OK starts autoplay with the best source of that resolution; All sources opens the usual list. Back cancels.
-A resolution typed in the search (in 4K, 1080p, UHD) is used straight away when there are sources in it; when there are none, the summary says so and asks.
-The resolution you choose is respected even with Autoplay SD Quality only switched on.
-Listings opened by the assistant (seasons, classic searches) open inside the Videos window, so Back goes up one level as usual.
[COLOR fffdb515]Settings > Personal Assistant[/COLOR]
-New section at the end of Settings.
-Welcome: switch the summary on or off, show it once per Kodi session or once a day, only when something needs attention, and close it automatically after 10, 20 or 30 seconds if you do not touch it.
-Your name: type it yourself, or let luc_kodi take it from your accounts, in this order: Trakt, PunchPlay, SIMKL, WeTrakr, MDBList, Real-Debrid, TorBox, AllDebrid, Premiumize. Found in your accounts shows the name it would use and where it came from. Values that are not a name (customer numbers, placeholders) are skipped, and for an email only the part before the @ is used.
-Search: Use the assistant in Search (off brings back the classic Search menu), Ask which resolution before playing (off plays the best source straight away, as autoplay does), Remember my last resolution, and Understand requests in your own words (Gemini; off sends everything to the title search).
-Title Search limit (Movies and TVShows), until now in General, and Clear search history, until now in Maintenance, have moved here. Your values are kept. Clear search history also clears the assistant's recent searches.
[COLOR fffdb515]No more "classes left in memory" in the log[/COLOR]
-After a playback or a browse, Kodi wrote that the add-on "has left several classes in memory that we couldn't clean up" (Window, Monitor, Player, PlayList, Addon, Dialog, DialogProgress, DialogProgressBG). The add-on made those Kodi objects as soon as it loaded and kept them for good, in control.py, in the scrapers' control.py, in the Up Next, Still Watching, Trakt manager and welcome windows, and in AIOStreams.
-They are now made the first time they are needed and dropped when the add-on finishes each run, so Kodi finds none left. Nothing changes in use: window properties, settings and dialogs work as before.
-Tasks of a run can still be working when it ends (scrapers that have not answered yet, the count behind the welcome window...). What they use is dropped as soon as the last of them finishes, and a progress bar that is still open on screen is never closed under them. The service drops its own when Kodi shuts down.
-With debug logging on, the log says what was released at the end of each run and which tasks were still running.
